Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1913: Kneeling on one knee with the other leg extended and toes up to stretch the hamstring and calf.
Kneel on one knee and extend the other leg in front, heel on the floor and toes pulled up.
Place your hands on the floor or the front thigh for support.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until you feel a pull behind the extended leg.
Keep the extended knee straight but not locked.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1914: Seated wide leg stretch that opens the inner thighs while lengthening the hamstrings.
Sit on the floor with your legs spread wide and knees straight.
Sit tall with your toes pointing up.
Hinge forward from the hips, walking your hands out in front of you.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the inner thighs and backs of the legs.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly, then sit back up.
og1915: A seated reach toward the toes that lengthens the hamstrings.
Sit on the floor with one leg straight out in front of you.
Reach toward your toes with a long back until you feel the back of the thigh stretch.
Keep your knee straight but not locked, and avoid rounding your back too much.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1916: A standing forward fold that stretches the hamstrings and calves.
Stand with your feet hip width apart.
Hinge at the hips and reach your hands down toward your shins or toes until you feel the back of the thighs stretch.
Let your head and neck hang relaxed and keep a slight bend in the knees.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1917: A standing forward fold with the legs crossed, which shifts the stretch to the back of the rear leg.
Stand tall and cross one foot over the other.
Hinge forward at the hips and reach toward the floor until the back of the thighs stretch.
Keep both legs fairly straight and let your head hang relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1918: A seated figure four style stretch for the buttocks and deep hip rotators.
Sit upright on the floor or a chair and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Gently press the raised knee down and lean your chest forward with a long back until the buttock stretches.
Keep your spine long instead of collapsing forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1919: A seated hip stretch with one leg folded in front and the other tucked behind you.
Sit on the floor with one leg bent in front of you and the other leg bent behind.
Lean your chest forward over the front shin until you feel the stretch deep in the hip and buttock.
Keep both sit bones as level as you can.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1920: Pointing the foot downward to stretch the front of the ankle and shin.
Sit on a chair or the floor with one leg extended.
Point your toes away from you as far as is comfortable.
Gently press the top of the foot with your hand for a little extra stretch.
Keep the movement slow and avoid forcing the ankle.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1921: Lying on your back, you lift one straight leg to stretch the hamstring with the lower back supported.
Lie on your back with both legs straight.
Lift one leg toward the ceiling, holding behind the thigh or calf.
Keep the knee as straight as is comfortable and the other leg flat on the floor.
Gently draw the leg toward you until you feel a pull behind the thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1922: A lying hamstring stretch where a towel around the foot lets you pull the leg closer without strain.
Lie on your back and loop a towel around the ball of one foot.
Raise that leg toward the ceiling, holding both ends of the towel.
Keep the knee nearly straight and the other leg flat on the floor.
Gently pull the towel until you feel a stretch behind the thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1923: A partner lifts your straight leg to deepen a relaxed hamstring stretch.
Lie on your back with your legs straight and relax completely.
Have a partner lift one leg by the heel, keeping the knee straight.
Tell your partner to stop when you feel a pull behind the thigh.
Keep your other leg and lower back flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.
og1924: Standing with the toes lifted against a surface to stretch the calf.
Stand facing a wall or step and place the ball of one foot against it with the heel on the floor.
Lean your hips gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the calf.
Keep your heel down and your back tall.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1925: Dropping one heel off a step to stretch the calf through a full range.
Stand on the edge of a step with the ball of one foot on it and hold a rail for balance.
Slowly lower that heel below the step until you feel the calf stretch.
Keep the knee straight to hit the calf, then bend it slightly to reach deeper into the soleus.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1926: A seated ankle stretch that lengthens the calf and the outer side of the lower leg.
Sit with one leg extended and hold the foot with your hand.
Point the foot down and turn the sole slightly outward.
Gently press the foot until you feel a stretch along the front and outer ankle.
Move slowly and stop at a mild stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1927: A seated ankle stretch that lengthens the front of the lower leg and the inner side of the ankle.
Sit with one leg extended and hold the foot with your hand.
Point the foot down and turn the sole slightly inward.
Gently press the foot until you feel a stretch along the front and inner ankle.
Move slowly and stop at a mild stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1928: A stretch using a wall bar to flex the ankle and lengthen the muscles of the lower leg.
Stand facing the wall bars and place the front of one foot against a low bar.
Lean your body forward and press your heel toward the floor until the lower leg stretches.
Hold the bars with your hands to stay balanced.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1929: A bent-knee stretch that targets the lower calf and the muscles around the shin.
Stand facing a wall with one foot back and the toes pressed against the wall or floor.
Bend the knee of the stretching leg slightly.
Shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch low in the calf.
Keep the heel on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1930: A deep crouch with the heels pressed back to stretch the calves and Achilles area.
Crouch down with your feet flat and hands on the floor for balance.
Shift one heel backward and press it toward the floor.
Keep the other leg bent and supporting your weight.
Feel the stretch in the calf of the pressing leg.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1931: A deep squat hold that opens the hips and loosens the knees and ankles.
Stand with your feet a little wider than your shoulders and toes turned slightly out.
Sink down into a deep squat and press your elbows against your inner knees to open the hips.
Keep your heels on the floor and your chest tall.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1932: A partner guides your bent knee toward your chest to stretch the hips and glutes while you stay relaxed.
Lie on your back with your legs straight and relax.
Have a partner bring one knee slowly toward your chest.
Tell them to stop when you feel a stretch in the hip and buttock.
Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.
og1933: A seated twist with one knee raised that stretches the hip and buttock.
Sit on the floor with one leg straight and the other knee bent, foot flat on the floor.
Cross the bent leg over the straight one, and rotate your torso toward the raised knee, hugging it with the opposite arm.
Sit tall and twist from the middle of your back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1934: A seated twist with the raised knee and the back leg extended, giving the hip a longer stretch.
Sit on the floor with one leg extended and the other knee bent and crossed over it.
Rotate your torso toward the bent knee, using the opposite elbow to guide it, until the hip stretches.
Keep your spine long and look over your back shoulder.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1935: Lying on your back and drawing a crossed knee up toward the opposite shoulder to stretch the glutes and hips.
Lie on your back with your knees bent.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the knee of the lower leg or behind the thigh and pull it up toward your chest.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1936: Lying on your back and guiding a crossed knee down across the body to stretch the outer hip and glutes.
Lie on your back with your knees bent.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Use your hand to guide the crossed knee gently down and across your body.
Keep your shoulders on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1937: Pulling a bent knee toward your chest to stretch the buttock muscles.
Sit on the floor with your legs out in front.
Bend one knee, hold it with both hands and gently pull it toward your chest.
Keep your back tall and avoid rounding it as you pull.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1938: A relaxed seated hip stretch with the front leg slightly bent, easy on the knee.
Sit on the floor with one leg slightly bent in front of you and the other leg folded comfortably.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long back until you feel the hip and buttock stretch.
Keep the knee of the front leg soft throughout.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1939: A lying stretch for the deep hip rotators and glutes, pulling the knee toward the chest.
Lie on your back and bend both knees.
Bring one knee toward your chest and turn it slightly outward.
Hold the shin and ankle and draw the leg closer.
Keep your lower back resting on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1940: A seated stretch pulling the foot toward the chest to open the hips and buttocks.
Sit on the floor with your back tall and legs extended.
Bend one knee and hold the foot and shin.
Pull the foot gently toward your chest while keeping your spine upright.
Feel the stretch deep in the buttock and hip.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1941: Crossing one leg behind the other and leaning aside to stretch the outer hip.
Stand tall and cross one leg behind the other, feet close together.
Lean your torso away from the back leg and push the hip out slightly until you feel the outer hip stretch.
Keep both feet flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1942: A standing side lean that stretches the iliotibial band along the outside of the thigh.
Stand next to a wall or support and cross your outer leg behind the other.
Lean your hips toward the wall and reach the outer arm overhead until the outside of the hip and thigh stretches.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1943: A yoga-style hip opener with one shin folded in front, stretching the glutes and the hip flexors of the back leg.
Start on hands and knees and slide one knee forward behind your wrist.
Extend the other leg straight behind you.
Lower your hips toward the floor and keep your chest tall.
Fold forward over the front leg for a deeper stretch if comfortable.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1944: A floor stretch for the deep hip rotators and buttock muscles.
Lie on your back with your knees bent.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee and pull the lower thigh toward your chest until the buttock stretches.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1946: A standing stretch drawing one knee up and in to open the hip and glutes.
Stand tall, holding a wall or support for balance.
Lift one knee and hold the shin and ankle with both hands.
Pull the leg gently toward your chest and slightly across the body.
Keep your standing leg soft and your back straight.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1947: A standing side stretch that lengthens the outer hip and thigh.
Stand next to a wall and cross one leg behind the other.
Push your hips sideways toward the wall.
Lean your upper body away from the hips until you feel the outer hip stretch.
Keep both feet flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1948: A seated rotation that works the hip through a twisting stretch.
Sit on the floor with your knees bent and both feet flat.
Let both knees drop to one side and rotate your torso the opposite way until you feel the hip stretch.
Keep your hands behind you for support.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1949: A standing lunge-style stretch for the front of the hip and thigh.
Stand and step one foot forward and the other back into a staggered stance.
Tuck your pelvis and squeeze the glute of the back leg.
Shift your hips slightly forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1951: A seated stretch that opens one hip by turning the leg outward.
Sit on the floor and bend one leg so the foot rests against the opposite thigh.
Lean your chest forward over the bent leg while pressing the knee toward the floor until the hip stretches.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1952: A partner-assisted leg movement that gently stretches the hip and thigh.
Lie on your back and relax.
Have a partner support one leg and gently extend it.
Let the partner move the leg only to a mild stretch.
Keep your lower back flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.
og1953: A supported standing quad stretch that also opens the front of the hip.
Stand tall holding a wall or chair for support.
Bend one knee and hold the ankle behind you.
Pull the heel toward your glutes and push the hip slightly forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1954: A quad stretch with the back foot resting on a box or bench, opening the front of the thigh.
Stand facing away from a box or bench and place the top of one foot on it behind you.
Stand tall on the front leg with a soft knee.
Tuck your pelvis and lower the hips slightly until you feel a stretch in the front of the thigh.
Hold a support for balance if needed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1955: Kneeling with one leg folded and leaning back to stretch the quadriceps.
Kneel on both knees, then lift one foot out in front so that the other leg is folded.
Place your hands behind you on the floor.
Lean back slowly until you feel a stretch in the front of the folded thigh.
Keep your hips lifted and avoid sagging into the lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1956: Sitting back on your heels and leaning back to stretch both quadriceps at once.
Kneel and sit back so your hips rest on your heels.
Place your hands on the floor behind you.
Lean back slowly and lift the hips slightly until you feel a stretch in the front of both thighs.
Stop if you feel any pinch in the knees.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then come back up slowly.
og1957: Standing with the top of the foot on the floor to stretch the muscles at the front of the shin.
Stand tall and hold a wall for balance.
Place the top of one foot on the floor behind you with the toes curled under.
Gently press the foot down by bending the standing knee.
Feel the stretch along the front of the shin and ankle.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1958: Pressing the tops of the toes against the floor to stretch the front of the foot and shin.
Stand next to a support and place the top of one foot on the floor behind you with the toes curled under.
Gently bend your standing knee and press the toes down until you feel the stretch on top of the foot and shin.
Keep the pressure light and controlled.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1959: A stretch with the foot raised on a support, easing the shin and top of the ankle.
Stand next to a wall and lift one foot behind you onto a low support with the top of the foot down.
Keep your torso upright and your standing leg soft.
Press your hips forward gently until you feel the shin stretch.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1960: Kneeling and sitting back onto your heels to stretch the front of the shins and ankles.
Kneel on a mat with your feet pointing straight back and the tops of the feet on the floor.
Slowly sit back toward your heels until you feel the shins and ankles stretch.
Place your hands on the floor in front of you to control the pressure.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1961: A deep squat on the balls of the feet that stretches the toes and the bottom of the feet.
Crouch down with your heels lifted and toes tucked under.
Place your hands on the floor in front of you for support.
Slowly sit back toward your heels until you feel the toes and soles stretch.
Ease off if the stretch is too sharp.
og1962: A seated stretch for the muscles that lift the toes, using your hand to point the toes downward.
Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the top of the foot and toes with your hand.
Gently curl the toes and foot downward until you feel a stretch on the top.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1963: Seated stretch combining pointing the toes down with a turn of the sole outward.
Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the top of the foot and toes with your hand.
Curl the toes down and turn the sole gently outward.
Feel the stretch along the top and outer edge of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1964: Seated stretch combining pointing the toes down with a turn of the sole inward.
Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the top of the foot and toes with your hand.
Curl the toes down and turn the sole gently inward.
Feel the stretch along the top and inner edge of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1965: A seated stretch pulling the toes back to lengthen the bottom of the foot.
Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the toes with your hand.
Gently pull the toes back toward your shin.
Feel the stretch along the sole of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1966: Seated stretch pulling the toes back while turning the sole outward.
Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the toes with your hand.
Pull the toes back toward your shin and turn the sole gently outward.
Feel the stretch along the sole and inner edge of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1967: Seated stretch pulling the toes back while turning the sole inward.
Sit and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the toes with your hand.
Pull the toes back toward your shin and turn the sole gently inward.
Feel the stretch along the sole and outer edge of the foot.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1968: Pulling the toes back against a wall to stretch the sole of the foot and the calf.
Stand facing a wall and place the toes of one foot on it with the heel on the floor.
Lean forward gently until you feel the stretch along the bottom of the foot and into the calf.
Keep your heel firmly on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1969: A gentle rocking stretch that improves ankle movement and loosens the calf.
Stand facing a wall with one foot forward, toes a few inches from it.
Keep your front heel on the floor.
Bend the front knee and glide it toward the wall.
Return and repeat slowly for 10-15 reps, then switch feet.
og1970: A tall standing stretch that opens the shoulders and chest.
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms and lift them gently away from your body.
Keep your chest open and your neck relaxed.
og1971: Clasping your hands behind your back and lifting them to open the front of the shoulders.
Stand tall and clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms and lift your hands up and away from your body until the shoulders and chest stretch.
Keep your chest open and avoid leaning forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1972: A seated stretch that opens the front of the shoulders using a bench.
Sit on the edge of a bench and place your hands behind you on it, fingers pointing back.
Walk your hips slightly forward off the bench.
Lower your hips gently until you feel a stretch at the front of the shoulders.
Keep your back close to the bench and shoulders down.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then rise up.
og1973: A partner gently draws your arms back to stretch the front of the shoulders.
Sit tall and put your arms behind you, palms facing down.
Have a partner stand behind and hold your wrists or forearms.
Ask them to lift your arms slowly until you feel a stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and chest open.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then lower slowly.
og1974: Standing with your hands clasped behind you to open the front of the shoulders.
Stand tall and clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lift your hands slightly away from your body.
Keep your chest up and avoid arching your lower back.
og1975: A seated stretch that lengthens the shoulder and chest by pressing the arms back and down.
Sit tall on a chair or bench.
Place your hands behind you on the seat, fingers pointing back.
Press your shoulders down and back, opening your chest.
Lean slightly forward until you feel the stretch.
og1976: Stretching one arm back and down to lengthen the front of the shoulder.
Stand next to a wall or post and place one hand on it behind you with the arm straight.
Slowly turn your body away until you feel the front of the shoulder stretch.
Keep the arm straight and the shoulder relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1977: Reaching one arm behind your back and pulling it across to stretch the shoulder.
Reach one arm behind your back.
Grab that wrist with the other hand and gently pull it across your body.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1978: A stretch for the back of the shoulder and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
Stand tall and extend one arm behind you.
Reach across to grab it with the other hand.
Draw the arm gently back and across the body.
Keep your chest open and your shoulders down.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1979: A cross body stretch that loosens the back of the shoulder and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
Stand or sit tall and bring one arm across your chest.
Use the opposite hand to press the arm toward you until the shoulder and upper back stretch.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1980: A classic cross-body stretch for the back of the shoulder.
Stand tall and bring one arm straight across your chest.
Use your other forearm to press the arm gently toward your body.
Keep the shoulder relaxed and down.
Feel the stretch in the back of the shoulder.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1981: A cross-body shoulder stretch with the elbow bent, easing the back of the shoulder.
Stand tall and bring one arm across your chest with the elbow bent.
Hold the elbow with your other hand.
Gently pull the elbow toward the opposite shoulder.
Keep your shoulders level and your neck relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1982: A gentle rotation stretch for the shoulder joint.
Stand tall and bend one elbow to 90 degrees at your side.
Slowly rotate your forearm outward or inward, using the other hand to assist, until you feel the shoulder stretch.
Keep your elbow tucked in close to your body.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1983: Reaching overhead to stretch the shoulders and the sides of the upper body.
Stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Reach one or both arms overhead and up as high as you can, then press them slightly backward.
Do not arch your lower back as you reach.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1984: A stretch aimed at the small stabilizing muscles around the shoulder joint.
Stand tall and bring one arm across your body at chest height.
Hold the arm just above the elbow with the other hand and draw it in until the back of the shoulder stretches.
Keep the shoulder blade down and relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1985: A stretch for the rotator cuff with the elbow lifted out to the side.
Stand tall and lift one elbow out to the side, hand behind your head.
Hold the elbow with your other hand.
Gently press the elbow back and slightly down.
Feel the stretch in the shoulder.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1986: An overhead stretch for the rotator cuff and back of the arm.
Raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow, palm resting on your upper back.
Use your other hand to hold the elbow.
Gently press the elbow back and down.
Keep your ribs down and chest open.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1987: A stretch for the rotator cuff with the arm held low behind the body.
Stand tall and place one arm behind your back, bent at the elbow.
Hold the wrist with the other hand.
Gently draw the hand away from your body and slightly up.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og1988: A kneeling stretch where you reach one arm across the body to open the back of the shoulder.
Kneel on a mat and slide one arm across the floor in front of you, palm down.
Sink your chest toward the floor and keep reaching until the shoulder and upper back stretch.
Keep your hips over your knees.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1989: A hanging stretch between parallel bars that opens the shoulders and lengthens the lats.
Stand between parallel bars and grip them at hip height.
Walk back slightly, letting your arms straighten.
Lower your chest toward the floor and press your head between your arms.
Feel the stretch in the lats and shoulders.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then walk forward to release.
og1990: A stretch that eases the shoulder into outward rotation.
Stand next to a doorframe and bend your elbow to 90 degrees with your forearm on the frame.
Slowly turn your body away from the arm until you feel the front of the shoulder stretch.
Keep your elbow level with your shoulder.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1991: A stretch that eases the shoulder into inward rotation.
Stand tall and place one hand behind your lower back with the elbow bent.
Use the other hand or a towel to gently draw the hand up your back until the back of the shoulder stretches.
Keep your shoulders level and do not twist.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og1992: A hack squat on a sled machine through a full range of motion, loading the quads and glutes.
Set your shoulders under the pads and your feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Unlock the safety and straighten your legs.
Lower your hips slowly until your thighs are below parallel.
Keep your back flat against the pad and knees tracking over your toes.
Press through your whole foot to stand back up.
og2071: A one-leg hip thrust that works the glutes hard and challenges balance and hip stability.
Sit with your upper back against a bench and one foot flat on the floor.
Extend the other leg or hold it up.
Drive through the heel to lift your hips until your body is flat.
Squeeze your glute at the top, then lower under control.
Complete the reps, then switch legs.
og2072: A glute-focused bridge with the upper back on a bench, lifting the hips to build strong glutes.
Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and knees bent.
Plant your feet flat, hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is level.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
og2087: A stretch for the back of the shoulder and the muscles along the upper back.
Stand tall and bring one arm across your chest.
Hold it with the other arm just above the elbow.
Gently pull while rounding the upper back slightly forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og2088: Using a towel behind the back to ease the shoulders into a deeper stretch.
Hold a towel in one hand and raise that arm overhead, bending the elbow.
Reach the other hand up from behind your back and grab the towel.
Gently pull the towel down with the lower hand.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og2089: A simple stretch that opens the fingers and forearm muscles, useful after typing or gripping.
Hold one arm out in front of you with the elbow straight.
Use the other hand to gently pull the fingers back until you feel a stretch in the palm and forearm.
Keep the fingers straight and relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
og2090: Clasped hands pressed forward with the palms facing out to stretch the forearms.
Stand or sit tall and interlace your fingers.
Turn your palms outward and straighten your arms in front of you.
Push your hands gently away until you feel the stretch in the forearms.
og2091: A stretch for the top of the forearm with the fingers pointing down.
Extend one arm in front of you with the palm facing down.
Bend the wrist so the fingers point toward the floor.
Use your other hand to press the back of the hand gently toward you.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og2092: Pressing the palm against a wall to stretch the forearm flexors.
Stand facing a wall and place one palm on it with the fingers pointing down.
Slowly turn your body away until you feel the stretch in the forearm.
Keep your fingers flat on the wall.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

og3310: The standard flat bench press with a loaded barbell, the staple lift for chest size and pressing strength.
Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar under control to your mid chest.
Press it back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your shoulder blades pinched and your feet planted throughout.
og3311: A front squat started from a rack or blocks height, so you begin the rep with the bar already set. It builds quad and trunk strength.
Set the bar on the blocks or rack at front shoulder height.
Step in, rest the bar on your front shoulders with elbows high.
Lift it off and stand tall with feet shoulder width apart.
Squat down with a tall chest until your thighs pass parallel.
Stand back up by driving through your feet, then re-rack the bar.
og3312: A weighted muscle up performed with the added load on a bar. An advanced pull and dip that trains the lats, chest and triceps.
Commence suspendu à une barre de traction, les paumes tournées vers l'extérieur et les mains légèrement plus écartées que la largeur des épaules.
Gaine ta sangle abdominale et tire tes omoplates vers le bas et l'arrière.
Plie tes coudes et tire ta poitrine vers la barre en gardant ton corps droit.
Une fois ta poitrine au niveau de la barre, pousse avec tes mains et ramène tes coudes vers l'arrière, en soulevant ton corps au-dessus de la barre.
Marque une pause en haut du mouvement, puis redescends lentement jusqu'à la position de départ.
Répète le nombre de répétitions souhaité.
og3313: A weighted dip on a straight bar or parallel bars. It builds the chest, triceps and shoulders with added resistance.
Positionne-toi entre des barres parallèles, les bras complètement tendus et le corps droit.
Abaisse ton corps en fléchissant tes coudes jusqu'à ce que le haut de tes bras soit parallèle au sol.
Marque une pause, puis repousse-toi vers le haut jusqu'à la position de départ en tendant tes bras.
Répète le nombre de répétitions souhaité.
og3314: A ring hold with the arms out and the legs straddled. It builds the chest and shoulders and is a stepping stone toward the full maltese.
Commence suspendu à une paire d'anneaux, les bras complètement tendus et le corps aligné.
Écarte largement les jambes, en formant une position en écart.
Gaine ta sangle abdominale et abaisse lentement ton corps jusqu'à ce que tes bras soient parallèles au sol.
Maintiens cette position pendant quelques secondes, puis repousse-toi jusqu'à la position de départ.
Répète le nombre de répétitions souhaité.
og3315: An advanced gymnastics hold on rings with the arms out wide and the body straight. It demands huge strength in the chest, shoulders and core.
Commence debout, les pieds écartés à la largeur des épaules et les bras tendus droit sur les côtés.
Penche-toi lentement vers l'avant, en gardant tes bras tendus, jusqu'à ce que le haut de ton corps soit parallèle au sol.
Gaine ta sangle abdominale et maintiens cette position pendant quelques secondes.
Reviens à la position de départ en poussant sur tes pieds et en te relevant.
Répète le nombre de répétitions souhaité.
og3316: A flowing series of barbell lifts done back to back without putting the bar down. It works your whole body and your conditioning.
Load a light to moderate barbell and stand over it with feet hip width apart.
Perform the first lift of your chosen sequence, such as a deadlift.
Move straight into the next lift without setting the bar down.
Keep each rep crisp with a braced core and a flat back.
Finish all lifts for one round, then lower the bar and rest before repeating.
og3317: A strongman event where you lift one side of a heavy vehicle and flip it over. It takes full body strength and leg drive.
Squat low at the edge of the vehicle with a flat back and hands underneath.
Brace your core and pull your chest up.
Drive hard through your legs and lift the edge to hip height.
Shift your hands and push up and over with your legs and arms.
Let it roll over fully, then step back and reset for the next flip.
og3318: A rotating movement that swings the arms and torso in a full circle. It gets the heart rate up and loosens the trunk.
Tiens-toi debout, les pieds écartés à la largeur des épaules et les genoux légèrement fléchis.
Tends les bras droit devant toi, parallèles au sol.
Gaine ta sangle abdominale et balance tes bras dans un mouvement circulaire, en faisant pivoter ton torse en même temps.
Continue le mouvement circulaire en balançant tes bras et en faisant pivoter ton torse pour le nombre de répétitions souhaité.
Pense à respirer tout au long de l'exercice.
og3319: A floor press with palms facing each other, which is kind to your shoulders. It trains the chest and triceps through a short range.
Lie on the floor with knees bent and a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing in.
Start with your upper arms resting on the floor.
Press the dumbbells straight up over your chest.
Pause briefly at the top without locking out hard.
Lower slowly until your triceps touch the floor and repeat.
og3320: A chest supported row on an incline bench with a neutral grip. It targets the mid back with little strain on your lower back.
Set a bench to a low incline and lie chest down on it with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang with palms facing each other.
Row both dumbbells toward your hips, leading with your elbows.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower slowly to full arm extension and repeat.
og3321: A band version of the reverse fly that works the back of your shoulders and upper back, handy for posture.
Hold the band in both hands in front of you with arms straight.
Stand tall with a soft knee bend and your core tight.
Pull your hands apart and out to the sides at shoulder height.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Return slowly to the start without letting the band snap back.
og3322: A beginner friendly deadlift with a kettlebell between your feet. It teaches the hip hinge and builds glutes and hamstrings.
Stand with feet hip width apart and the kettlebell between your feet.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to grab the handle with both hands.
Keep your chest up and back flat.
Drive through your feet and stand tall, squeezing your glutes.
Hinge back down to set the kettlebell on the floor and repeat.
og3323: The first half of a turkish get up, moving from lying to a seated position with the kettlebell overhead. It builds shoulder stability and core strength.
Lie on your back with a kettlebell pressed up in one hand and the same side knee bent.
Keep your eyes on the bell and your arm vertical.
Roll onto the opposite elbow, then onto your hand.
Come up to a tall seated position with your arm still locked overhead.
Reverse the steps slowly to lie back down, then switch sides.
og3324: An alternating band press angled upward, with a torso twist added to bring in your core. It works the upper chest and trunk together.
Anchor a band low behind you and hold the handles at chest height.
Stand in a split stance with your core braced.
Press one hand up and forward while rotating your torso slightly.
Return under control and press with the other arm.
Keep your hips steady and alternate sides for the full set.
og3325: An alternating band row with a rotation, training your back and the muscles that twist your trunk.
Anchor a band in front of you at low height and hold both handles.
Stand in a staggered stance with arms extended.
Pull one handle back toward your hip while rotating your torso.
Squeeze your shoulder blade, then return slowly.
Repeat with the other arm and keep alternating.
og3326: A standing band pulldown done one arm at a time with a trunk twist. It trains your lats and adds core work.
Anchor a band high in front of you and hold both handles with arms overhead.
Stand tall in a staggered stance.
Pull one handle down toward your ribs while rotating your torso.
Keep your elbow tucked and shoulder down.
Return slowly and switch to the other arm.
og3327: A push-up from the planche position with the feet off the ground. It is an elite bodyweight move for the chest, shoulders and triceps.
Commence en position de pompe, les mains posées un peu plus écartées que la largeur des épaules.
Gaine ta sangle abdominale et abaisse ton corps vers le sol, en gardant tes coudes près de tes flancs.
En te baissant, penche ton corps vers l'avant et décolle tes pieds du sol en t'équilibrant sur tes mains.
Continue à abaisser ton corps jusqu'à ce que ta poitrine soit juste au-dessus du sol.
Pousse à travers tes mains et étends tes bras pour ramener ton corps vers le haut jusqu'à la position de départ.
Maintiens une ligne droite de ta tête à tes talons pendant tout le mouvement.
Répète le nombre de répétitions souhaité.
og3328: A barbell complex that links a stiff leg deadlift into a clean and then a step. It builds posterior chain power and rhythm.
Stand holding a light barbell with an overhand grip at thigh height.
Lower the bar down your legs with soft knees and a flat back.
Stand up, then pull the bar explosively and catch it on your shoulders.
Take a controlled step forward with the bar racked.
Step back, lower the bar and begin the next round.
og3329: A sit up on a roman chair that gives you a big range of motion for your abs and hip flexors.
Sit on the roman chair with your feet locked under the pads.
Cross your arms over your chest and lean back slightly.
Curl your torso up until your chest nears your thighs.
Pause at the top and keep your neck relaxed.
Lower back slowly under control and repeat.
og3330: A side crunch combined with a bent knee lift. It trains the obliques and lower abs together.
Lie on your back with your hands by your head and knees bent.
Lift your shoulders and knees at the same time.
Twist and bring one elbow toward the opposite knee.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
og3331: A twisting crunch with your legs lifted straight, making your core work harder through the lever.
Lie on your back with legs raised straight and hands by your head.
Lift your shoulders off the floor.
Rotate to bring one elbow toward the opposite hip.
Keep your legs steady and low back pressed down.
og3332: A crunch over a stability ball while holding a weight, using the ball for a longer range of motion in your abs.
Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet out until your back is supported.
Hold a weight against your chest.
Let your torso drape back over the ball for a full stretch.
Curl up until your upper back clears the ball.
Lower slowly back into the stretch and repeat.
og3333: A one arm dumbbell bench press with a wide elbow path, stressing the chest while your core resists rotation.
Lie on a bench with one dumbbell held over your chest.
Place your free arm on your stomach or out to the side.
Lower the dumbbell with elbow flared out until you feel a chest stretch.
Press it back up over your chest.
Keep your torso square, then switch arms after the set.
og3334: A one arm fly lying on the floor, a safe way to stretch and load the chest with a limited range.
Lie on the floor with knees bent and a dumbbell in one hand over your chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow.
Open your arm out to the side until your upper arm touches the floor.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbell back above you.
Finish all reps, then switch arms.
og3335: A loaded hip bridge that targets your glutes. Resting a dumbbell on your hips adds resistance.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell across your hips.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.
og3336: A v up while holding a dumbbell, raising your arms and legs together to challenge the abs.
Lie flat with legs straight and a dumbbell held in both hands overhead.
Lift your arms and legs together, forming a V shape.
Touch the dumbbell near your shins.
Lower back down slowly without dropping your legs.
og3337: A side plank with a dumbbell held on your hip or raised overhead. It trains the obliques and lateral stability.
Lie on one side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs stacked.
Hold a dumbbell on your top hip.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds without sagging.
Lower, then repeat on the other side.
og3338: A single leg hinge holding a dumbbell, which trains your hamstrings, glutes and balance.
Stand on one leg with a dumbbell in the opposite hand or both hands.
Keep a soft bend in your standing knee.
Hinge forward while your free leg extends behind you.
Lower the dumbbell toward the floor with a flat back.
Squeeze your glute to stand back up, then switch legs.
og3339: A lunge holding a dumbbell in one hand. The uneven load makes your core work to keep you balanced.
Stand tall holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
Step forward into a long stride.
Lower your back knee toward the floor, keeping your torso upright.
Push through your front foot to return to standing.
Alternate legs and switch the dumbbell hand halfway.
og3340: A hip hinge with nearly straight legs holding dumbbells. It stretches and strengthens the hamstrings and glutes.
Stand with feet hip width apart holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Keep your knees slightly bent and back flat.
Push your hips back and slide the dumbbells down your legs.
Stop when you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
og3341: A dumbbell lunge variation for leg strength and balance, working quads and glutes.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Step forward into a long stride.
Bend both knees until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and torso upright.
Push back to the start and switch legs.
og3342: A cable raise that moves your arms into a Y shape, building the shoulders and the muscles that stabilise your shoulder blades.
Set the pulleys low and hold a handle in each hand, arms crossed in front.
Stand tall with a slight lean forward.
Raise both arms up and out into a Y shape.
Keep your thumbs pointing up and shoulders down.
og3343: A machine lateral raise that isolates the side delts with smooth, guided resistance.
Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine pivots.
Sit tall and place your arms against the pads.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Lower slowly without letting the weights rest.
og3344: A machine crossover that brings your arms together across the body, isolating the chest.
Set the seat height and grip the handles with a slight elbow bend.
Sit tall with your back against the pad.
Sweep your arms together in front of your chest.
Squeeze your chest at the center.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch.
og3345: A wrist curl using a hand grip spring, strengthening your forearms and grip.
Sit with a forearm resting on your thigh or a bench, palm up.
Hold the hand spring in that hand.
Squeeze the handles together by curling your wrist and fingers.
Release slowly, finish your reps, then switch hands.
og3347: Curl the dumbbells and keep going into an overhead press, training the arms and shoulders in one smooth rep.
Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward.
Curl both weights up to shoulder height without swinging.
Rotate your wrists slightly and press the weights overhead.
Lower to your shoulders, then back down to your sides.
Brace your core and keep your ribs down.
og3348: A plank on an incline where you tap each shoulder, building core and shoulder stability.
Place your hands on a bench or box and extend into a plank position.
Spread your feet slightly wider for balance.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Keep your hips level and body in a straight line.
Alternate sides at a steady pace.
og3349: A squat with a cable held at your chest, keeping you upright while the quads and glutes work.
Set the cable low and hold the handle at your chest.
Step back to create tension and stand with feet shoulder width apart.
Sit down and back into a squat with your chest tall.
Descend until your thighs are parallel.
og3350: A sideways lunge against cable tension, training glutes, inner thighs and side to side strength.
Hold a low cable handle at your chest and stand sideways to the stack.
Step wide to one side and sit back into that hip.
Keep the other leg straight and feet flat.
Push off your bent leg to return to center.
Complete the reps, then switch sides.
og3351: A lunge with cable resistance, building leg strength with a constant load.
Hold a cable handle at chest height and step away from the stack.
Step forward into a long stride.
Lower your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your torso upright and front heel down.
Push back to standing and alternate legs.
og3352: A kneeling hip hinge with a cable pulled between your legs. It teaches the hinge and trains glutes with little spinal load.
Kneel facing away from a low cable with a rope held between your legs.
Sit your hips back with a flat back.
Let the rope pull your hands back between your knees.
Drive your hips forward to a tall kneeling position.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and repeat.
og3353: A single arm overhead extension on a high pulley that stretches and loads the long head of the triceps.
Face away from a high pulley and hold the handle overhead with one hand.
Stand in a split stance with your elbow pointing up.
Extend your arm forward and up until it is straight.
Return slowly and switch arms after the set.
og3354: A second take on the cable front squat, holding the handle at your chest to stay upright and hit the quads.
Set the cable low and hold the handle against your chest.
Stand with feet shoulder width apart.
Sit down into a deep squat, chest tall.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
Press through your heels back to standing.
og3355: A second variation of the cable side lunge for the glutes and inner thighs.
Hold a cable handle at chest height, standing sideways to the stack.
Step wide to the side and bend that knee.
Push your hips back and keep your chest up.
Push off the bent leg to return.
Finish your reps, then switch sides.
og3356: A forward stepping lunge with cable tension, working quads and glutes.
Hold a low cable handle at your chest and stand facing away from the stack.
Drop your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your front knee stable over the ankle.
Push back to the start and switch legs.
og3357: A floor seated cable row using a rope, which lets you pull the hands apart and squeeze the mid back.
Sit on the floor facing a low cable with legs extended and the rope in your hands.
Sit tall with a straight back.
Pull the rope toward your lower chest, spreading your hands.
Extend your arms slowly and repeat.
og3358: A lat pulldown done from the floor with a neutral grip, focusing on the lats.
Kneel or sit on the floor under a high cable with a parallel grip handle.
Sit tall and lean back slightly.
Pull the handle down to your upper chest.
Drive your elbows down and back.
Return slowly to full arm extension.
og3359: A standing press with cables that trains the chest while your core keeps you steady.
Set the cables at chest height and hold a handle in each hand.
Step forward into a split stance.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight.
Squeeze your chest at the end.
og3360: A crawl on hands and feet with the knees hovering off the floor. It works the shoulders, core and legs together.

Décolle légèrement tes genoux du sol, en gardant ton dos plat et ta sangle abdominale gainée.
Avance simultanément ta main droite et ton pied gauche, puis ta main gauche et ton pied droit.
Continue à ramper vers l'avant en alternant les mouvements de tes mains et de tes pieds.
Maintiens un rythme régulier et garde ta sangle abdominale contractée pendant tout l'exercice.
Continue sur la distance ou la durée souhaitée.
og3361: A side-to-side hop that mimics a speed skater, landing on one foot at a time. It builds leg power and balance.
Tiens-toi debout, les pieds écartés à la largeur des épaules.
Fléchis légèrement les genoux et saute vers la droite en atterrissant sur ton pied droit.
À l'atterrissage, balance ta jambe gauche derrière ta jambe droite et touche le sol avec les orteils de ton pied gauche.
Saute immédiatement vers la gauche, en atterrissant sur ton pied gauche.
À l'atterrissage, balance ta jambe droite derrière ta jambe gauche et touche le sol avec les orteils de ton pied droit.
Continue à alterner les côtés, en sautant et en touchant le sol avec chaque jambe.
Répète le nombre de répétitions souhaité.
og3362: A close grip press lying down with a cable, putting emphasis on the triceps.
Lie on a bench with the cable behind your head and hold the handle with a narrow grip.
Start with arms bent over your chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
Keep your elbows close to your body.
og3363: A standing close grip cable press that focuses on the triceps.
Set the cable at chest height and hold the handle with a narrow grip.
Stand in a split stance, core tight.
Press forward until your arms are straight.
og3364: A seated close grip cable press for the triceps with a stable base.
Sit on a bench facing away from a cable at chest height.
Hold the handle with a narrow grip.
Press forward until your arms are straight.
Keep your back against the pad.
og3365: A deep bodyweight squat variation that builds leg strength and hip mobility.
Stand with feet slightly wider than your shoulders and toes turned out.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Sit your hips down and back into a deep squat.
Pause at the bottom without rounding your back.
Drive through your feet to stand up.
og3366: A single-leg squat with the back foot held behind you, demanding strong quads and good balance.
Stand on one leg and bend the other knee, holding that foot behind you.
Reach your free arm forward for balance.
Lower slowly until the back knee lightly touches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to stand.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.
og3367: A single-leg squat with the free leg swept behind, like a speed skater, for leg strength and balance.
Stand on one leg with the other knee bent and the foot lifted behind you.
Swing your arms forward for balance.
Sit your hips back and lower on the standing leg.
Lightly tap the back knee near the floor.
Stand up through the front foot, then switch legs after your reps.
og3368: A hip driven swing using a dumbbell, building power in your glutes and hamstrings.
Stand with feet wider than hips and hold one dumbbell in both hands.
Hinge at the hips and swing the dumbbell between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to swing it to chest height.
Guide it back down and hinge into the next rep.
og3369: Squatting while whipping the battle ropes with alternating arms. It raises your heart rate and works legs and shoulders.
Hold one rope end in each hand and stand with feet shoulder width apart.
Whip the ropes up and down with alternating arms.
Keep your chest tall and your knees stable.
Continue for a set time at a steady pace.
og3370: A high energy move combining a jump squat with alternating rope waves. It builds power and conditioning.
Hold the rope ends and stand in a squat position.
Start waving the ropes with alternating arms.
Jump up explosively and land softly.
Go straight into the next squat.
Keep going for a set time and rest when needed.
og3371: Swinging the ropes from side to side to condition your shoulders and trunk.
Hold the rope ends in an athletic stance with knees bent.
Swing both ropes to one side.
Swing them across to the other side in a flowing motion.
Rotate through your torso a little.
Keep a steady rhythm for the set time.
og3372: Side lunges while whipping the ropes alternately, working legs, shoulders and heart.
Hold the rope ends and stand with feet together.
Step wide to one side and sit into a side lunge.
Whip the ropes alternately with your arms.
Alternate sides and keep the waves going.
og3373: Drawing circles with the ropes toward each other. It builds shoulder endurance.
Stand with knees bent and a rope end in each hand.
Move your arms in circles that turn inward.
Keep the circles even and large.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Continue for a set time then rest.
og3374: Drawing outward circles with the ropes, training shoulders and conditioning.
Stand with knees bent and a rope end in each hand.
Move your arms in circles that turn outward.
Keep the movement smooth and even.
og3375: Sweeping the ropes out and in like a fly, hitting the shoulders and upper body.
Stand with knees bent, a rope end in each hand and arms in front.
Sweep your arms out wide and slightly up.
Bring them back together in front of you.
og3376: A jumping jack with rope waves added, so arms and legs both work hard.
Hold the rope ends with feet together.
Jump your feet apart while raising your arms and making waves.
Keep a steady pace for the set time.
og3377: A seated twist where you swing the ropes side to side. It trains the obliques and conditioning.
Sit on the floor with knees bent and lean back slightly.
Hold the rope ends in front of you.
Twist your torso to one side and swing the ropes.
Keep your chest lifted and continue for the set time.
og3378: Jumping lunges while waving the ropes, a demanding mix of power and cardio.
Hold the rope ends and stand in a split stance.
Start making waves with your arms.
Jump and switch legs in mid air.
Keep switching for the set time.
og3379: Big overhead wave style rope slams that fire up the shoulders and heart.
Stand with feet shoulder width apart and a rope end in each hand.
Raise both arms overhead and slam the ropes down.
Repeat quickly to make big waves.
Keep your core braced for the set time.
og3380: Alternating or double low waves with heavy ropes that spike your heart rate and work the shoulders, arms and core.
Hold one rope end in each hand and stand in a quarter squat.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Whip the ropes down and up so waves travel low along the floor.
Keep the waves even and your hips stable.
Work for 20-30 seconds at a hard pace.
Rest, then repeat for several rounds.
og3381: Pull your chest up to the underside of a sturdy table to train the back and arms using your own weight.
Lie under a sturdy table and grip the edge with both hands.
Extend your legs with heels on the floor and body in a straight line.
Pull your chest toward the table edge, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower with control until your arms are straight.
Keep your hips up the whole time.
og3382: An easier inverted row with bent knees, pulling up to a sturdy table to build back strength.
Lie under a sturdy table and grip the edge with both hands.
Bend your knees and plant your feet on the floor.
Lift your hips so your body forms a line from knees to shoulders.
Pull your chest to the table edge, squeezing your shoulder blades.
og3383: A pike push-up with your feet on a bench, loading the shoulders more than a flat push-up does.
Place your feet on a bench and your hands on the floor, hips piked high.
Walk your hands back until your body forms an inverted V.
Bend your elbows and lower your head toward the floor.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees from your body.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
og3384: An explosive overhead rope slam that builds conditioning and power through the whole body.
Hold a rope end in each hand and stand in an athletic stance.
Raise both ropes overhead while rising onto your toes.
Slam them down hard while dropping into a squat.
Keep your back flat and your core braced.
Reset and repeat at a steady, powerful pace.
og3385: A seated machine press that loads the thighs and glutes with a stable path.
Sit on the machine and set your back firmly against the pad.
Place your feet on the platform about shoulder-width apart.
Release the safety and lower the weight until your knees bend to about 90 degrees.
Press through your whole foot to extend your legs.
Stop just short of locking your knees.
og3386: A machine isolation move for the front of the thighs.
Sit on the machine with your back against the pad.
Hook your lower shins under the roller and align your knees with the pivot.
Extend your legs until they are nearly straight.
Squeeze your quads briefly at the top.
Lower slowly back to the start.
Avoid swinging or lifting your hips.
og3387: Bodyweight dips using two sturdy chairs, working the triceps and chest.
Place two sturdy chairs facing each other and brace them against a wall.
Grip the seats, lift your body and straighten your arms.
Lower yourself by bending your elbows until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Keep your elbows pointing back and your chest up.
Make sure the chairs cannot slide.
og3388: A bodyweight row under a sturdy support between two chairs for the upper back and arms.
Set a sturdy bar or table edge between two stable chairs and lie under it.
Grip the support with straight arms and your body in a plank line.
Pull your chest toward the support.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
Keep your hips up the whole time.
og3389: A sit-up with your feet or legs supported on a chair to focus on the abs.
Lie on your back and rest your lower legs on a chair seat, knees bent.
Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands by your ears.
Curl your torso up toward your knees.
Do not pull on your neck.
og3390: A calf raise from a raised step with a chair for balance, giving a deeper stretch and fuller range.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a step edge, holding a chair for balance.
Let your heels drop below the step to stretch your calves.
Rise as high onto your toes as you can.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly into the deep stretch.
og3391: A standing bent-over rotation that mobilizes the spine and works the obliques.
Stand with feet wide and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back.
Extend your arms out to the sides.
Rotate your torso and reach one hand toward the opposite foot.
Return through the middle and twist to the other side.
Move with control and keep your hips square.
og3392: A close-stance squat with your heels raised on a small step to emphasize the quads.
Stand with your heels on a low platform and your feet close together.
Hold your arms in front for balance.

Lie on your back with one knee bent, foot flat, and the other leg extended or raised.
Rest a dumbbell across your hips and hold it steady.
Drive through the planted heel and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
Squeeze your glute at the top for a second.
Lower with control and repeat, then switch legs.
og4292: Lying face down, you curl a dumbbell held between your feet toward your glutes. A simple way to train the back of the thighs without a machine.
Lie face down on a bench and grip the edge for support.
Have a dumbbell gripped between your feet, or placed by a partner, with legs straight.
Bend your knees and curl the weight toward your glutes.
Pause briefly at the top without lifting your hips.
Lower slowly until your legs are almost straight.
og4293: A hip hinge with nearly straight legs and dumbbells. It stretches and strengthens the hamstrings, glutes and lower back.
Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Keep your legs almost straight with a soft knee and a flat back.
Push your hips back and lower the weights along your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes.
og4294: A deep squat performed with your arms locked out overhead. It trains the legs while testing shoulder and hip mobility.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and raise both arms straight overhead.
Brace your core and keep your arms in line with your ears.
Sit your hips back and down into a deep squat, chest tall.
Drive through your heels to stand, keeping your arms locked overhead.
og4295: Lunging forward step after step with a dumbbell in each hand. It builds leg and glute strength and balance.

Step forward with one leg and lower until both knees are about 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee over your ankle.
Push through the front foot and bring the back leg forward into the next step.

og4296: A kneeling lunge stretch with a cross-body reach to deepen the stretch along the front of the hip.

Reach the arm on the kneeling side up and across toward the opposite side.
Shift your hips gently forward until you feel the stretch at the front of the hip.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og4299: A stretch for the front of the thigh done lying on your side or front. It loosens tight quads after leg work.

Pull your heel toward your glutes while keeping your knees close together.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
og4300: A standing stretch for the front of the thigh. Easy to do anywhere to ease tight quads.

Bend one knee and grab the ankle behind you.
Pull your heel toward your glutes, keeping your knees together and hips square.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.
og4307: A seated rotation with your arms held straight out, loosening the spine and working the waist gently.

Rotate your torso slowly to one side, keeping your spine long.

og4309: A pilates move where you alternate pulling one knee in while the other leg extends. It builds core control and coordination.

Place your hands on one shin and extend the other leg out low.

og4310: A pilates exercise where you scissor your straight legs while holding the raised one. It trains the abs and tests hamstring flexibility.

Extend one leg straight up and the other hovering low.

og4312: A standing side-leaning stretch that opens up the lats and the side of the torso.

Raise one arm overhead and keep the other hand resting on your hip.
Lean slowly toward the opposite side, lengthening along the raised arm.

og4314: A gentle back stretch draped over or kneeling at a stability ball. It lengthens the spine and relaxes the torso.

Roll the ball forward as you sink your hips back.

Roll the ball back in to come up.
og4315: A seated pilates stretch where you round forward over your legs, one vertebra at a time. It mobilizes the spine and stretches the hamstrings.

Flex your feet and lift your torso up out of your hips.
Curl your chin to your chest and round forward, reaching past your toes.

og4318: A pullover lying on the floor, which limits the stretch range and keeps the focus on the lats and chest.

Lower the weight in an arc behind your head until your upper arms touch the floor.
Pull it back over your chest using your lats.
Keep your ribs down and core tight throughout.
og4322: A bodyweight side bend with one arm bent behind your head, working the obliques.

Squeeze your side to return upright.

og4326: A pullover with the elbows kept bent, lying on a bench. It stretches and strengthens the chest and lats.

Pull the dumbbell back over your chest and repeat.
og4327: A leg press on a sled that moves straight up, pressing the weight vertically. It loads the thighs and glutes heavily.

Lower under control for each rep.
og4328: A quick jumping drill where your legs swap front and back like scissors. Good for conditioning and coordination.
Stand tall with one foot forward and one back, arms ready.
Hop lightly and switch your leg positions in the air.

Land softly on the balls of your feet.

og4329: A push-up variation with hands on a sturdy chair. It makes pressing easier while still training chest and arms.

Walk your feet back until your body is straight.

Push back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your core tight and hips level.
og4330: A reverse crunch finished with a leg kick upward, hitting the lower abs.

Curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest.

og4331: A crunch where one leg lifts as you curl up. It adds a lower-abs challenge to the basic crunch.

Curl your shoulders up toward your hips.

og4332: A crunch held at the top to keep the abs under tension. Simple and burns quickly.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or across your chest.
Curl your head and shoulders off the floor.

og4333: A bench reverse crunch where your knees trace a circle. It works the lower abs and obliques.

Curl your hips up and draw a small circle with your knees.

og4334: A side plank with a knee-to-elbow crunch. It trains the obliques and shoulder stability together.

Extend back to the side plank position.

og4335: A weighted side bend using a dumbbell to load the obliques.

Bend sideways toward the weighted side, keeping your hips still.

og4336: A biceps curl on a plate-loaded lever machine that guides the path. It builds the front of the upper arm.

Squeeze your biceps at the top.

og4338: A barbell curl done chest-down on an incline bench, which removes swinging and isolates the biceps.

og4339: A pullover with a barbell lying on a bench. It stretches and strengthens the lats and chest.

og4340: A pullover using a wider grip, which spreads the load across the lats and chest.

og4341: Raising one dumbbell at a time in front of you to shoulder height. It targets the front of the shoulders.

og4342: A dumbbell fly where you rotate your wrists through the movement for a stronger chest squeeze.

og4346: A standing overhead press without weight, good for learning the pressing path or warming up.

og4348: A four-point hold on hands and knees where you engage the abs. A gentle way to learn core bracing.

og4349: A one-legged squat with a barbell on your back. It builds leg strength and balance, so use light weight.

og4365: A resting yoga pose that gently stretches the back and hips, similar to child pose.

og4366: A standing crunch where you lift a knee to the side toward your elbow. It works the obliques.

og4367: A bent-over row with a cable using an underhand grip, which emphasizes the lower lats and biceps.

og4369: A light, no-equipment biceps curl using self-resistance, useful for warming up.

Tense your biceps at the top.
og4370: A seated calf raise with a barbell on a Smith machine, working the lower calf muscle.

Lower slowly for a full stretch.
og4371: A one-armed incline press on a plate-loaded lever machine. It trains the upper chest one side at a time.

og4374: A standing cable fly from a low pulley, sweeping the arms up and across one at a time. It trains the upper chest.

og4375: Circle a medicine ball around your head to warm up the shoulders and challenge your core and balance.

og4382: A forward lunge with the bar resting on your front shoulders. The front load works the quads and glutes and challenges your core.

og4403: A wide-stance deadlift with a kettlebell or two that trains the glutes, inner thighs and legs.

Bend sideways at the waist, reaching over with the raised arm.

og4811: A side plank hold, a second variation. It strengthens the obliques and the muscles that keep your trunk stable.
Lie on your side and prop yourself on your forearm under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Keep your neck neutral and your core tight.
Lower down and repeat on the other side.
og4812: A side crunch, a second variation, aimed at the obliques. It shortens the side of the waist with a small controlled movement.
Lie on your side with knees bent and one hand behind your head.
Rest the other hand on the floor for balance.
Lift your shoulders and knees toward each other.
Squeeze the side of your waist at the top.
Complete your reps, then switch sides.
og4816: A goblet squat with a two-second pause in the bottom. The pause builds leg strength and control out of the hole.

Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly out.
Squat down with your chest tall until your thighs are at least parallel.

Drive through your heels to stand.
og4817: A hip hinge with a kettlebell held at the chest. It strengthens the hamstrings, glutes and lower back.
Hold a kettlebell by the horns against your chest.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back and hinge forward with a flat back.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes to stand tall again.
og4818: A ring row with the feet raised, making the bodyweight pull harder. It builds the upper back and biceps.

Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower with control without letting your hips sag.
og4819: Lying on your back with heels in the rings, you bridge up and curl your feet in. It hits the hamstrings hard.

Lift your hips into a bridge.
Bend your knees to pull your heels toward your glutes.
Keep your hips high the whole time.
Extend your legs slowly to return.
og4820: A hanging or reclined rollout that drives the knees in under the rings. It strongly trains the lower abs and core.
Set up in a push-up position with your feet in the ring straps.
Keep your arms straight and shoulders over your hands.
Pull your knees toward your chest by curling your pelvis.
Pause with your hips lifted and abs tight.
Extend your legs back to a straight plank slowly.
og4821: A single-leg step-up onto a bench with dumbbells at your sides. It builds leg strength and balance.
Stand facing a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Place one foot fully on the bench.
Press through that heel to stand up on the bench.
Lower your other foot back down slowly.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.
og4822: A Romanian deadlift that finishes with an explosive jump and shrug. It trains power through the hips and traps.

Hinge your hips back and lower the weights along your legs with a flat back.

Reset into the hinge and repeat.
og4824: A fast, rotating punch that travels across the body. It raises your heart rate and trains shoulders, core and rotation.

Rotate your hips and torso as you throw a punch across your body.
Extend your arm fully and pivot your back foot.
Alternate sides at a brisk, controlled pace.
og4825: A face-down stretch with arms reaching out, opening the chest and front of the shoulders.

Draw your shoulder blades together and back.
Keep your neck in a neutral position.
og4826: Lying on your back, you raise one leg at a time. It works the lower abs and hip flexors.

Press your lower back into the floor.
Raise one leg up toward the ceiling.
Lower it slowly while lifting the other leg.

og4829: Skipping rope with a jump on each turn. It builds stamina, coordination and calf strength.

Swing the rope over your head using your wrists.

og4830: A push-up performed from a kneeling child's pose position. It trains the chest and triceps with a gentle range.
Kneel and sit back on your heels with your arms stretched forward.
Place your hands on the floor at chest height.
Shift forward and lower your chest between your hands.
Push the floor away to rise.
Sit back to the starting pose and repeat.
og4831: A floor pulldown where you slide your hands on a towel from overhead to your sides. It works the lats without any equipment.
Kneel with your hands on a towel placed on a smooth floor, arms stretched forward.

Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Slide back out slowly to the start.
og4832: Lying face down, you raise light dumbbells out to the sides. It targets the rear shoulders and upper back.

Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
og4833: A one-arm Arnold press with a rotating grip. It works all heads of the shoulder while challenging core stability.

og4835: A dumbbell bench press where your grip rotates during the press. It adds a smooth, shoulder-friendly path for the chest.
