Shift your weight forward until you feel the stretch at the front of the hip.
Raise the arm on the kneeling side overhead.
og6772: A standing stretch for the muscles on the outside of the lower leg. It helps ankle mobility.
Stand near a wall for balance.
Cross one foot behind and turn the sole so the outer edge presses into the floor.
Gently shift your weight onto that foot.
Feel the stretch along the outside of the lower leg.
og6773: A standing stretch for the muscle at the front of the shin. Useful after running or lots of walking.
Stand near a wall for balance.
Place the top of one foot on the floor behind you with toes curled under.
Gently bend the standing knee to press forward.
Feel the stretch along the shin.
og6774: A seated stretch that opens the space between the shoulder blades. It relieves tightness in the upper back.
Sit tall and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Push your arms forward and round your upper back.
Tuck your chin slightly and spread the shoulder blades apart.
Hold for 20-30 seconds while breathing steadily.
og6775: A standing drill that wakes up the small muscles of the feet. It builds foot control and balance.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Spread your toes wide and press all of them into the floor.
Lift your toes while keeping the ball of the foot down.
og6776: A one-arm cable row with a high elbow. It focuses on the rear delts and upper back.
Set a cable at chest height and grab the handle with one hand.
Stand with feet staggered and your torso slightly braced.
Pull the handle toward you with your elbow flared out.
Squeeze the rear shoulder at the end.
Extend slowly, then switch arms after your reps.
og6785: A seated move pushing the knees outward against a band. It strengthens the outer hips and glutes.
Sit tall on a bench with a band around your thighs above the knees.
Keep your feet flat and planted.
Press your knees apart against the band.
Hold for a second at the widest point.
Bring the knees back together slowly.
og6786: A gentle hip check where the ankle rests on the opposite knee and the knee drops out. It shows how mobile the hip is.
Lie on your back with legs straight.
Place one foot on the opposite knee.
Let the bent knee drop out to the side.
Relax and notice how far it goes.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without forcing it.
og6787: A simple check of how far the hip turns outward. You do it gently to see your range.
Sit or lie with the knee bent 90 degrees.
Swing the lower leg inward so the hip rotates outward.
Stop where you feel a stretch or end of range.
Note how far each side goes.
og6788: A simple check of how far the hip turns inward. You do it gently to see your range.
Sit or lie with the knee bent 90 degrees.
Swing the lower leg outward so the hip rotates inward.
Stop where you feel a stretch or end of range.
Note how far each side goes.
og6789: A lying check comparing the length of both legs. It is done gently and with a relaxed body.
Lie flat on your back with legs straight and feet together.
Compare the position of your heels or ankles.
Bend your knees and lift your hips, then lower and straighten again.
og6790: A simple check of how far the shoulder turns outward. Move slowly and stay in a pain-free range.
Stand or lie with your elbow bent 90 degrees and tucked at your side.
Keep your elbow against your body.
Stop where you feel a stretch or end of range.
Note how far each side goes.
og6791: A simple check of how far your shoulder turns inward, handy for spotting tightness before you train.
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Reach one arm behind your back with the palm facing out.
Slide your hand slowly up your spine as far as is comfortable.
Note how high your thumb reaches, keeping your chest open.
Lower the arm, then repeat with the other side to compare.
og6792: A quick posture check to see whether one shoulder sits higher than the other.
Stand relaxed with your feet hip-width apart and arms hanging loose.
Look straight ahead and let your shoulders settle naturally.
Check in a mirror, or ask a friend, whether both shoulders are at the same height.
Roll the shoulders once and re-check without shrugging.
Note any difference and repeat now and then to track it.
og6793: A forward-fold style check of how flexible the back of your body is, from calves up to your lower back.
Stand with your feet together and your knees straight.
Hinge at the hips and slowly reach down toward your toes.
Let your head and arms hang relaxed without bouncing.
Note how far your fingertips reach.
Rise slowly, rolling up one vertebra at a time.
og6794: A hip flexor length test where you lie on the edge of a bench and see how freely the thigh hangs.
Sit at the end of a bench, then lie back and hug one knee to your chest.
Let the other leg hang off the edge with the thigh relaxed.
Keep your lower back flat on the bench.
Notice whether the hanging thigh rises above the bench or the knee straightens.
og6795: The frontal-view version of the Thomas test, checking for tight hip flexors and inner thighs while you lie on a bench.
Sit at the end of a bench and lie back, pulling one knee to your chest.
Let the other leg hang down off the edge, fully relaxed.
Keep your lower back pressed down and your pelvis still.
Watch whether the hanging leg drifts outward or the thigh lifts.
og6796: A wide-stance squat on the smith machine down to a chair. The seat gives a consistent depth.
Place a chair behind you and set the bar on your upper back.
Take a wide stance with toes turned out.
Sit back and down until you lightly touch the chair.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your heels to stand up.
og6797: A sideways step up onto a bench with a barbell on the back. It builds single-leg strength in the quads and glutes.
Place the bar on your upper back and stand beside a bench.
Put the inside foot flat on the bench.
Press through that heel and stand up on the bench.
Lower the other foot back down under control.
Complete your reps, then switch sides.
og6798: A standing band kickback that builds the glutes while challenging your balance on one leg.
Loop the band around your ankles or hold it under your standing foot.
Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee and brace your abs.
Kick the other leg straight back against the band.
Squeeze your glute at the top without arching your lower back.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og6799: A lying V-up to the side while holding a dumbbell. It works the abs and obliques hard.
Lie on your back holding a dumbbell with both hands overhead.
Lift your legs and torso together, angling toward one side.
Reach the dumbbell toward your feet.
og6800: A seated combo that pairs an overhead press with a Russian twist, feet off the floor. It challenges the trunk and shoulders together.
Sit leaning back slightly with knees bent and feet off the floor.
Lower them, then twist your torso to one side.
Twist to the other side and repeat the sequence.
og6801: A seated overhead press combined with in and out leg movements. It works the shoulders and the lower abs together.
Sit on the floor leaning back slightly, dumbbells at your shoulders.
Pull your knees in, then extend the legs out as the weights stay up.
Lower the dumbbells to your shoulders.
Repeat, keeping your back long and core braced.
og6802: You hold dumbbells overhead while raising the legs alternately. It trains the lower abs and shoulder stability.
Sit on the floor leaning back a little and press the dumbbells overhead.
Keep your arms locked and steady.
Raise one leg off the floor.
Lower it and raise the other leg.
Keep alternating, then lower the weights.
og6803: A seated in and out leg drill that goes to the side and then to the front. It works the abs and obliques.
Sit on the floor leaning back, hands behind you for support.
Lift your feet off the floor with knees bent.
Extend your legs out to one side and pull them back in.
Extend them straight in front and pull back in.
Repeat the pattern on the other side.
og6804: From a plank you alternately pull one arm up toward your chest as if climbing. It builds core stability and shoulder control.
Start in a forearm or high plank with your body in a straight line.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Pull one arm up and back toward your ribs.
Return it to the floor under control.
Alternate arms without rocking your hips.
og6805: A V-up where one arm and the opposite leg meet, holding a dumbbell. It trains the abs through a big range.
Lie on your back with a dumbbell in each hand, arms overhead.
Lift your torso and one leg at the same time.
Reach the weights toward your raised foot.
og6806: A variation of the seated overhead press and Russian twist combo with feet off the floor. It works the trunk and shoulders.
Sit leaning back slightly with knees bent and feet off the floor.
Press both dumbbells overhead and lower them.
Twist your torso to one side, then the other.
Keep your chest tall and breathe steadily.
og6809: A sit-up holding a dumbbell overhead with the legs resting on a bench. The extra reach makes the abs work harder.
Lie on the floor with calves resting on a bench, knees bent.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest or overhead.
Curl up into a sit-up, keeping your arms extended.
Reach toward your knees at the top.
og6810: A lying knee raise against band resistance. It builds the lower abs and hip flexors.
Lie on your back with a band looped around your feet or anchored.
Place your hands by your sides and brace your core.
Bring your knees toward your chest against the band.
Lower your feet slowly without arching your back.
og6811: A gentle release for the muscle under the shoulder blade using a stick for leverage. It helps the shoulder feel looser.
Hold a stick in one hand and bend your elbow to 90 degrees.
Place the other hand on the stick and rotate the arm outward.
Gently push into a comfortable stretch.
Release and repeat on the other arm.
og6812: A seated move using a ball to wake up the inner upper thigh. It works the pectineus and the nearby adductors.
Sit tall on a chair with a ball between your knees.
Place your feet flat and keep your back straight.
Squeeze the ball gently with your thighs.
og6813: The barbell bench press seen from the side to check bar path and form. It builds the chest, shoulders and triceps.
Lie on a bench with your eyes under the bar and feet planted.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack it.
Lower the bar to your mid chest with elbows at about 45 degrees.
Touch lightly and press back up over your shoulders.
Keep your shoulder blades pinched throughout.
og6820: A fly on an incline bench using kettlebells. It stretches and works the upper chest.
Lie on an incline bench holding a kettlebell in each hand above your chest.
Keep a soft bend in the elbows.
Open your arms wide in an arc until you feel a chest stretch.
Squeeze the chest to bring the weights back together.
Control the weights and keep your wrists stable.
og6833: A seated side raise using kettlebells. It isolates the side delts without leg drive.
Sit upright on a bench holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
og6878: A calm cross-legged seat that opens the hips and teaches you to sit tall.
Sit on the floor and bend your knees.
Place one heel against your inner thigh and the other foot in front of it.
Rest your hands on your knees and lengthen your spine.
Relax your shoulders and look straight ahead.
Switch the cross of your legs and repeat.
og6879: An inversion where your forearms and head share the load, building shoulder strength and balance.
Kneel and place your forearms on the mat with your fingers interlaced.
Set the crown of your head lightly on the floor against your hands.
Lift your knees and walk your feet toward your face.
Lift your legs slowly, using your core, until they point to the ceiling.
Keep most of the weight in your forearms and shoulders.
Hold briefly, then lower with control and rest in child's pose.
og6880: A forearm balance that builds strong shoulders and core, also known as feathered peacock pose.
Start on your forearms and knees with your elbows under your shoulders.
Press your forearms into the floor and tuck your toes.
Lift your hips high and walk your feet toward your elbows.
Swing or float one leg up, then bring the other to meet it.
Keep your ribs in and your gaze between your hands.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
og6881: A machine pulldown where the arms cross the body path. It builds the lats and upper back.
Adjust the seat and thigh pad, then grab the handles.
Sit tall with your chest up.
Pull the handles down and across toward your torso.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Return slowly to a full stretch.
og6890: An overhead press done seated on the floor with legs straight. The position removes leg drive and demands a strong core.
Sit on the floor with legs extended and dumbbells at your shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your back tall.
Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower them to your shoulders under control.
Avoid leaning back during the press.
og6891: A seated floor press that alternates arms, which adds anti-lean trunk work. It trains the shoulders and the core.
Sit on the floor with legs extended, dumbbells at your shoulders.
Brace your core and sit tall.
Lower it and press the other arm.
Keep alternating without tilting your torso.
og6901: A gentle spinal extension from all fours that wakes up the back and often pairs with cat pose.
Start on hands and knees, with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale and let your belly drop toward the floor.
Lift your chest and tailbone while your gaze goes slightly forward.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
og6902: A seated pose that stretches the shoulders, triceps and hips together.
Sit with one knee stacked over the other and your feet beside your hips.
Reach one arm up and bend the elbow, hand down your back.
Sweep the other arm behind you and try to clasp your fingers.
Keep your spine tall and your chest open.
og6910: A push-up between parallel bars that lets you sink deeper than the floor allows. It gives the chest a greater stretch.
Grip two parallel bars and hold a straight plank position.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees.
Lower your chest below the level of your hands.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your body in one line throughout.
og6913: A seated drill squeezing the shoulder blades together. It strengthens the muscles that support good posture.
Sit tall with arms relaxed at your sides or held in front.
Pull your shoulder blades together and slightly down.
og6914: A variation of the seated shoulder blade squeeze with the arms held out. It strengthens the upper back and posture muscles.
Sit tall with elbows bent and hands by your ribs.
Draw your elbows back and pinch your shoulder blades together.
og6944: A standing or floor drill that copies the front crawl arm stroke. It raises your heart rate and warms the shoulders.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Swing one arm forward and over in a crawl stroke.
Alternate arms in a smooth, continuous rhythm.
Rotate your torso slightly with each stroke.
Keep going at a steady pace for 30-60 seconds.
og6958: A side-to-side jump over a low hurdle. It builds explosive power and quick landings.
Stand beside a low hurdle with feet together.
Swing your arms and jump sideways over it.
Land softly on both feet with knees bent.
Jump straight back over the other way.
Keep your ground contact quick and controlled.
og6959: A push-up with a band supporting the body to make the rep easier. It helps you build toward full push-ups.
Anchor a band across a rack or set of bars at chest height.
Rest your torso on the band in a plank position.
Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows at 45 degrees.
Press up using the bounce of the band as help.
Keep your body in a straight line.
og6961: A pull-up with the hands at different heights or one hand doing more work. It gently trains one-arm pulling strength.
Hang from the bar with one hand higher or on a towel and the other lower.
Brace your core and pull your chest up.
Lead with the working arm and pull your chin toward the bar.
Switch the hand positions on the next set.
og6964: A standing dumbbell press that adds upper back extension, training shoulder strength and posture together.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the dumbbells at shoulder height.
Brace your abs and lift your chest tall.
Press the dumbbells overhead while gently extending your upper back.
Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back.
Lower to your shoulders with control.
og6982: A full push-up focusing on wrist position and control. It builds the chest while preparing the wrists for load.
Start in a plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Spread your fingers and keep your wrists stacked.
Lower your chest to the floor under control.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
og6986: A wall-assisted version of a downward dog push-up with a push off at the top. It trains the shoulders in a bent-hip position.
Stand facing a wall and place your hands on it with hips back.
Lower your head toward the wall, bending the elbows.
Push explosively away from the wall.
Land softly back into the start position.
Keep your core braced and back flat.
og7019: A kneeling rollout with the forearms on a stability ball. It builds deep core strength.
Kneel facing a stability ball with your forearms resting on top.
Brace your abs and keep your hips in line with your back.
Roll the ball forward, extending your body.
Stop before your lower back sags.
Pull the ball back in using your abs.
og7054: A standing twisting move holding a dumbbell that works the forearm rotators. It builds wrist and grip strength.
Stand holding a dumbbell by its handle in front of you.
Keep your elbows bent and close to your sides.
Rotate your forearms and wrists inward and outward.
Move slowly through the full range.
og7055: A standing twisting move holding a plate that works the forearm rotators. It builds wrist and grip strength.
Stand holding a plate at its sides in front of you.
Keep your elbows bent and close to your sides.
Rotate the plate left and right using your wrists and forearms.
og7056: A standing reverse curl that ends with a forearm rotation. It targets the forearms and brachialis.
Stand holding dumbbells with an overhand grip at your thighs.
Curl the weights up while keeping your elbows tucked.
At the top, rotate your forearms so the palms turn up.
Keep your wrists strong and avoid swinging.
og7107: A machine press done with one leg at a time. It helps fix strength imbalances between legs.
Sit in the machine and put one foot on the platform.
Keep your back against the pad.
Press the platform away until your leg is almost straight.
Lower slowly until your knee bends to about 90 degrees.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.
og7108: A machine leg extension that isolates the front of the thigh. It builds quad size and strength.
Sit with your back against the pad and shins behind the roller.
Align your knees with the machine pivot.
Extend your legs until they are nearly straight.
Squeeze your quads at the top.
og7113: A pullover variation with straight arms that stretches and works the chest and lats through a long arc.
Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell above your chest with straight arms.
Keep a slight softness in your elbows and brace your core.
Lower the weight in an arc back over your head until you feel a stretch.
Keep your ribs down and your hips on the bench.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest.
og7114: A vertical pull with an EZ bar that builds the side shoulders and upper traps.
Stand tall holding the EZ bar with a shoulder-width grip.
Let the bar hang in front of your thighs.
Pull it up along your body, leading with your elbows.
Stop around chest height without shrugging hard.
Lower the bar slowly to the start.
og7129: A floor hamstring curl using your own weight, alternating legs to keep it easy on the joints.
Lie face down with your legs straight and your forehead on your hands.
Bend one knee and bring the heel toward your glute.
Squeeze the back of your thigh at the top.
og7154: A lateral shuffle where each step brings the knee high. It raises your heart rate and builds agility.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Shuffle sideways for a few steps.
Lift your knees high with each step.
Stay light on your feet and pump your arms.
Change direction and continue for 30-60 seconds.
og7155: A seated shrug with the cable pulling from behind the body. It trains the traps and the upper back.
Sit with a low cable behind you, holding the handle behind your back.
Keep your arms straight and chest tall.
Shrug your shoulders up and slightly back.
og7175: Gliding on inline skates for steady cardio that also works the legs and balance.
Put on skates, helmet and pads, and stand with your knees slightly bent.
Push one skate out to the side and glide on the other.
Alternate pushes with a relaxed arm swing.
Keep your chest up and your weight over the skates.
Skate at a steady pace for 10-30 minutes.
og7176: A seated machine calf press that pushes through the balls of the feet. It builds the calf muscles.
Sit in the machine and place the balls of your feet on the platform.
Press up as high as you can onto your toes.
Lower your heels slowly for a good stretch.
og7177: A seated machine press working one calf at a time to build lower leg strength.
Sit in the machine and place the ball of one foot on the platform.
Rest the other foot on the floor or the support.
Press up through your toes as high as you can.
Lower your heel slowly for a full stretch.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og7194: A quick hopping drill that crosses the feet and steps back, building agility and leg power.
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your knees soft.
Hop and cross one foot in front of the other.
Hop back out, then step one foot back behind you.
Land softly on the balls of your feet each time.
Alternate sides for the planned time.
og7198: A glute bridge with a band around the knees, pressing out to light up the side glutes.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and the band just above your knees.
Press through your heels to lift your hips.
At the top, push your knees apart against the band.
og7199: A lying hip abduction with bent knees that targets the outer hip and glutes.
Lie on your side with the band above your knees and your knees bent.
Stack your hips and rest your head on your arm.
Lift your top knee up against the band without rolling back.
Keep your feet together like a clamshell.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og7200: A seated band move pressing the knees apart to work the outer hips.
Sit tall on a bench or chair with the band just above your knees.
Plant your feet flat and hip-width apart.
Press your knees out against the band.
Hold briefly at the widest point.
og7201: A leg raise with band tension that challenges the lower abs and hip flexors.
Lie on your back with the band around your feet or anchored behind your head.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Raise your legs together toward the ceiling.
Lower them slowly without arching your back.
og7202: A side lunge with band tension that works the legs and hips from a different angle.
Stand with the band under your feet or around your thighs, feet together.
Sit your hips back and bend that knee, keeping the other leg straight.
Keep your chest up and your heel down.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og7203: A squat that steps sideways against a band, firing up the glutes and hips.
Place the band around your thighs and stand with feet hip-width.
Sit into a squat and stay low.
Step one foot out to the side against the band.
Bring the other foot in to follow.
Take several steps, then return the other way.
og7204: A second take on the band glute kickback, balancing on one leg while the other presses back.
Place the band around your ankles and stand tall on one leg.
Hold a wall or rail for balance if needed.
Keep a slight bend in your standing knee.
Kick the other leg back, squeezing the glute.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og7205: A squat jump with a band around the thighs to keep the knees driving outward.
Place the band above your knees and stand with feet shoulder-width.
Squat down with your chest up.
Land softly, absorbing into the next squat.
Keep your knees pressing out against the band.
og7206: A sideways step into a squat with band tension to train the glutes and legs.
Put the band around your thighs and stand tall.
Step one foot out to the side.
Stand up and bring your feet together.
Keep the knees from caving in.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og7207: A single-leg squat with the rear foot elevated and a band adding resistance.
Stand in front of a bench, band under your front foot and held at your shoulders.
Rest the top of your back foot on the bench.
Lower straight down until your front thigh is parallel.
Press through your front heel to rise.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og7208: A kneeling donkey-kick style move with band resistance for the glutes.
Start on hands and knees with the band around your foot and hands.
Keep your back flat and your core braced.
Kick one leg straight back and up.
Squeeze your glute at the top.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og7209: A kneeling leg sweep against a band that works the glutes and outer hips.
Start on hands and knees with the band around your thighs or foot.
Lift one leg out to the side with a bent knee.
Sweep it in a half circle, back and up.
Keep your hips level and your core tight.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og7210: A plank with jumping feet and a band around the legs, working your core while the hips resist.
Place the band above your knees and get into a high plank.
Brace your abs and keep your hips level.
Keep your hands under your shoulders.
og7211: A face-down hip extension combined with outward leg movement against a band.
Lie face down with the band around your ankles.
Rest your forehead on your hands.
Lift both legs slightly off the floor.
Open your legs out against the band.
Bring them back together and lower slowly.
Keep the movement small and controlled.
og7212: An air bike crunch with band tension for extra work on the abs and hips.
Lie on your back, hands behind your head, band around your feet.
Lift your shoulders and bring one knee toward your chest.
Rotate your opposite elbow toward that knee.
Extend the other leg against the band.
og7213: A light rotation exercise lying on your side that turns the arm inward. It strengthens the rotator cuff gently.
Lie on your side with your elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked to your ribs.
Rest the forearm on the floor in front of you.
Rotate your forearm up toward your belly.
Lower it slowly back to the floor.
Finish your reps, then switch sides.
og7216: A wall-supported raise of the opposite arm and leg. It trains balance and lower back stability.
Stand facing a wall in a bent over position with your hands on it.
Lift one arm and the opposite leg at the same time.
Hold for a second without twisting.
Lower and repeat on the other side.
og7217: A face-down raise with the arms out to form a T. It strengthens the muscles between the shoulder blades.
Lie face down with your arms out to the sides in a T.
Keep your forehead near the floor and neck neutral.
Lift your arms off the floor by pinching your shoulder blades.
Hold for a second at the top.
og7228: A pull-up on rings with a wide grip. The unstable rings make the lats and stabilizers work harder.
Grab the rings with a wide overhand grip and hang with arms straight.
Pull your chest toward the rings, driving elbows down and out.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
og7229: From a plank you slide a kettlebell under your body from one hand to the other. It works the core and shoulder stability.
Start in a high plank with a kettlebell beside one hand.
Spread your feet wide for balance.
Grab the kettlebell and slide it across under your body.
Place it down on the other side.
Keep your hips level and repeat in the other direction.
og7230: A wide-stance row between two kettlebells, alternating arms. It trains the lats and the core.
Place two kettlebells on the floor between your wide stance.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grab both handles.
Row one kettlebell to your hip while the other stays down.
Lower it and row the other side.
Keep your hips and shoulders square.
og7231: A chest-supported raise on an incline bench to a Y position with one arm. It builds the lower traps and rear delts.
Lie face down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in one hand.
Let the arm hang straight down.
Raise your arm forward and up in a Y shape, thumb up.
Lower slowly and switch arms after your reps.
og7232: A standing drill that moves the shoulder blades in circles. It improves shoulder mobility and control.
Stand tall with arms relaxed at your sides.
Lift your shoulders up toward your ears.
Bring them forward and up again in a circle.
Reverse the direction after several reps.
og7233: A standing shoulder blade rotation that warms up the upper back and improves control of the scapulae.
Stand tall with your arms at your sides.
Roll them back and down in a smooth circle.
og7234: Light dumbbell rotation that strengthens the small muscles behind the shoulder and between the shoulder blades.
Stand tall holding a light dumbbell with your elbow bent at 90 degrees and tucked at your side.
Keep your upper arm still and your shoulder blade pulled back and down.
Rotate your forearm outward as far as you comfortably can.
Pause briefly, then slowly return to the start.
Finish all reps, then switch arms.
og7235: A light dumbbell rotation that trains the rear shoulder and rotator cuff.
Stand tall holding a light dumbbell with your elbow tucked and bent to 90 degrees.
Keep your upper arm against your side.
Rotate your forearm outward, away from your body.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
og7237: Deadlift using a hook grip, where the thumb is trapped under the fingers, for a secure hold on heavy pulls.
Stand with the bar over mid-foot and grip it with your thumbs under your fingers.
Hinge down, brace your core and keep your back flat.
Push the floor away and stand up, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Lock out with hips and knees extended.
Lower the bar under control by hinging at the hips first.
og7251: Hanging straight-body raise toward a front lever position that challenges your abs and lats.
Hang from a pull-up bar with a firm grip.
Pull your shoulders down and tighten your core.
Raise your straight body up toward horizontal, keeping your arms straight.
Hold the top position for a moment.
og7252: Raise performed lying face down on an incline bench, hitting the rear delts and the small rotator muscles.
Lie chest down on an incline bench holding a light dumbbell in one hand.
Let the arm hang straight below your shoulder.
Raise the dumbbell out to the side, leading with your elbow, up to shoulder height.
Complete your reps and switch sides.
og7255: Sit-up started from a seated frog position, with knees out and soles together, to work the abs and open the hips.
Sit on the floor with the soles of your feet together and knees dropped out.
Lower your back halfway to the floor under control.
Pause, then lower fully to lie flat.
